name: r9-vectors-host-envelope
note: Envelopes and results between hosts (delegated host-work II.4.2, II.4.4; host-work-v1 §11.5). Each object is {body, sig, enc, ct}: the body signed by the sender's host_key (Ed25519) over enc(["atem-envelope-v1" or "atem-result-v1", jcs(body)]); the plaintext sealed with RFC 9180 base mode, DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305, empty AAD, to the recipient's host encryption key, info = enc(["atem-envelope-seal-v1" or "atem-result-seal-v1", account_id, genesis_hash (32 bytes), sender.host_id, u64(sender.host_trust_gen), recipient.host_id, u64(recipient.host_trust_gen), enc_kid, id, u64(created_at), u64(expires_at)]); sealed_hash = SHA-256(enc([enc, ct])). The sender's ephemeral is DeriveKeyPair(ikmE), ikmE = SHA-256(enc(["atem-r9-test-ikm", ikm_label])). Device lists: log L of r9-vectors-membership-log followed by `chain`, labels of `entries` (signed by dev-mac); the objects are signed at B = L + M7..M10 (head 10) unless their signed_at_head says otherwise. Objects: `signed_with` names the r9-vectors-keys host key whose signature `sig` is; `built` objects are what seal_envelope / seal_result make from the body's fields, `sealed.plaintext` and ikmE; `sealed` gives the seal's inputs and outputs (`plaintext`, or `plaintext_bytes` and `plaintext_sha256` over 4 KiB); `sealed_from` names the object whose sealed part it carries, `edited_from` the object it is after a change made after signing. Checks: `call` (open_envelope, or accept_result with `outbox`, the sending host's row) on L + `chain`, by `receiver` (its host_id, current host_trust_gen and the keys it accepts, r9-vectors-keys names), at `now`; `expect` is the verdict: open or accepted (with `sender`; the plaintext is the object's), not_delivered (with `sender` and the return grant's detail as `reason`), pending (the claimed host_id and host_trust_gen), refused (before the copy is shown to be the sender's, signed and intact (step 4): `reason` and `evidence` = SHA-256(enc([jcs(body), sig, enc, ct])), enc and ct empty when absent; it claims no id) or refused_authenticated (after it: the object's id and `reason`; it claims the id for its authenticated sender, (sender.host_id, id)).

objects.label: complete

objects.label: request_over

objects.label: gen2_before_add_host

objects.label: ids_mismatch

objects.label: plaintext_null
objects.note: a cancel plaintext holding a null member; no builder seals it

objects.label: plaintext_not_canonical
objects.note: a cancel plaintext whose members aren't in canonical order; the builder seals only the canonical form

objects.label: bad_times
objects.note: a cancel whose expires_at equals its created_at

objects.label: lifetime_too_long
objects.note: a cancel that expires 24 h and 1 ms after its created_at

objects.label: cancel_to_new_key
objects.note: a cancel sealed to host-b's new key host-b-enc-2, signed at the head of B + M11_rotate_b (seq 11), where host-a's list has the rotation

objects.label: cancel_to_a
objects.note: a cancel from host-b to host-a, sealed to host-a-enc-1

objects.label: evil_cancel
objects.note: a cancel from host-evil to host-b at B's head (seq 10, host-evil's add_host)

objects.label: evil_at_head_9
objects.note: a cancel from host-evil to host-b signed at seq 9, before host-evil's add_host

objects.label: removed_head_ahead
objects.note: a cancel by host-a at generation 1, signed at the head of B + M11_revoke_a + M12_readmit_a (seq 12)

objects.label: resigned
objects.note: host-evil strips the request and re-signs it as its own (sender host-evil): its signature verifies, but the seal's info binds host-a. Its verdict claims (host-evil, id), never host-a's (host-a, id): host-a's own request, judged after it, still opens (request_opens)

objects.label: resigned_keeping_sender
objects.note: host-evil re-signs the request's body as it is (sender host-a)

objects.label: head_ahead_bad_signature
objects.note: head_ahead's body signed by host-b's key: host-a's at generation 1 is known, so the signature is checked before waiting

objects.label: redirected_edited
objects.note: the request with its recipient changed to host-a (and host-a's enc_kid) after signing

objects.label: tampered_sealed_hash
objects.note: the request with its body's sealed_hash changed (to the cancel's) after signing

objects.label: tampered_ct
objects.note: the request with a byte of its ciphertext changed after signing: not the sender's copy

objects.label: head_ahead_tampered_ct
objects.note: head_ahead with a byte of its ciphertext changed after signing: a variant of a known sender's waiting object

objects.label: bare
objects.note: the request without its sealed part

objects.label: status
objects.note: host-b's receipt for the request: stored

objects.label: refusal
objects.note: host-b refused the cancel envelope at check 5 or 6

objects.label: result
objects.note: the agent's reply to the request's task, as reply_query returns it once submitted

objects.label: evil_status
objects.note: a status for the request from host-evil, a host of the account the outbox row didn't go to

objects.label: status_head_ahead
objects.note: host-b's status for the request, signed at the head of B + M11_revoke_a + M12_readmit_a (seq 12)

objects.label: dropped_reply
objects.note: a result whose reply the host dropped (no text left); no builder seals it
